items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Joe Maini was an incredible reader, same kind of reader as Stan Getz... I know, what a funny guy, he and Joe Maini used to work together and they were hysterical.

ctx.x: Yeah, I mean, when I played it decades later it still was really challenging and still sounded – especially the Handy charts, the Eddie Finckel charts were good, the Johnny Richards things I didn’t care for too much.

I never liked playing his music, it was incredibly hard but again Johnny Richards was one of those guys who had unbelievable technique. He really knew how to write his orchestra. I just didn’t find it fun to play. I tried out for his big band once when I was still playing trumpet and just fell on my can and I’d asked him before, I asked the manager, “Is it a hard book?” He said, “It’s the hardest book in the business.” I said, “Oh, come on,” [laughs] I found out it was the hardest book in the business. And I…
You know you mentioned just in passing Ellington and I know that you thought very highly of Ellington and Basie, we should talk about that.
